project.name: Air-Gapped Python Sandbox MCP Server
project.version_source_of_truth: config.VERSION (reported over MCP serverInfo.version; mirrored in README.md version history)
project.goal: Stateful offline Python code-interpreter exposed to an LLM over MCP, backed by a portable Python, for math/data/charts/document-parsing with no internet and no pip.
project.status: complete and verified; work is packaging/hardening/docs

source_duplication.note: Every server module exists at repo root AND under dist/AirGappedPySandbox/mcp-server/. They must stay identical.
source_duplication.rule: edit repo-root first, then copy into the package

modules.config.py: settings + env overrides; PROJECT_ROOT, WORKSPACE_DIR, KERNEL_PYTHON, timeouts, ensure_workspace()
modules.kernel_manager.py: StatefulKernel (cross-interpreter launch; timeout->interrupt->restart) + KernelPool/POOL (per-namespace kernels, warm reserve, idle eviction, LRU cap); KERNEL kept for test_core only
modules.server.py: FastMCP tools + _RULES + _format_response + _resolve_workspace_file (existing file) + _resolve_new_workspace_path (file to create) + _display_paths + main()

mcp_tools.name: write_workspace_file
mcp_tools.output: write_status SUCCESS|ERROR + file line + artifact link + run_python_file hint for .py
mcp_tools.namespace: not taken (no state; workspace is shared)
mcp_tools.why: removes the self-referential 'python that writes its own source' pattern that breaks small/mid-size models
mcp_tools.isolation: _resolve_new_workspace_path: containment checked on the parent after resolve(); rejects absolute paths, '..', Windows reserved device names, escapes
mcp_tools.overwrite_policy: refuses by default (user uploads share the directory); refusal states the fix

mcp_tools.name: install_python_packages

input.packages: str (names separated by spaces/commas; version specifiers allowed; URLs/paths/flags refused)

mcp_tools.output: install_status INSTALLED|FAILED|RUNNING + packages with versions + index/venv/timing + next_action
mcp_tools.runs_in: background thread; the tool answers within SANDBOX_TOOL_BUDGET and returns RUNNING (not a failure) with the exact arguments to resend, which joins the same job rather than starting a second pip
mcp_tools.installs_into: config.VENV_DIR, a venv from KERNEL_PYTHON with --system-site-packages; never the portable Python
mcp_tools.verified_by: the kernel itself via importlib.metadata, not pip's exit code
mcp_tools.failure_diagnosis: probe_index()/effective_index() separate unreachable index, plain-http index dropped as untrusted, and package genuinely absent

mcp_tools.name: reset_kernel_state
mcp_tools.output: restarts ONE namespace kernel; clears its memory, keeps files, other namespaces untouched

namespace_routing.why: AnythingLLM shares one MCP process across all conversations; one kernel meant cross-conversation variable-name collisions
namespace_routing.reinforcement: namespace is a required param; every response echoes 'active_namespace: ns-XXXX' banner + trailing reminder
namespace_routing.execution: one StatefulKernel per namespace via kernel_manager.KernelPool (singleton POOL)
namespace_routing.warm_reserve: POOL.prewarm() boots one spare; new namespace adopts it (first call ~0.06s); maintainer replenishes
namespace_routing.idle_eviction: maintainer sweeps every 30s, evicts namespaces idle > NS_IDLE_TIMEOUT
namespace_routing.lru_cap: MAX_NAMESPACES live kernels max; LRU evicted over cap
namespace_routing.workspace: files SHARED across namespaces (uploads work); only in-memory state isolated
known_limits: continuity breaks if model drops the tag after context truncation
weak target LLM copies tags less reliably
real fix = AnythingLLM sending conversation id via _meta (hook ready)

SANDBOX_TOOL_BUDGET.meaning: max time ONE tool call may block before answering; must stay under the MCP client's own request timeout (60s in the official SDK) or the client cancels first and the user sees 'Context server request timeout'

SANDBOX_EXEC_TIMEOUT.meaning: per-call execution timeout; kept under SANDBOX_TOOL_BUDGET. Was 60, which raced the client's 60s timeout

SANDBOX_NS_IDLE_TIMEOUT.meaning: evict idle namespace kernels after this

SANDBOX_MAX_NAMESPACES.meaning: max simultaneous namespace kernels; LRU eviction over cap

SANDBOX_PIP_INDEX_URL.meaning: intranet PyPI mirror for install_python_packages; unset means pip falls back to pip.ini/public PyPI, so installs fail on a closed network

SANDBOX_PIP_TRUSTED_HOST.meaning: host of a plain-http mirror; without it pip SILENTLY ignores the index

SANDBOX_VENV.meaning: venv installed packages go into; never inside the workspace

SANDBOX_PIP_RETRIES.meaning: 0 so a misconfigured mirror fails in a second instead of stalling for minutes
